summary: Brazil's first round happened yesterday: Flavio Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula (about 47 to 44 percent with 98 percent counted) and both advance to an October 25 runoff. Polymarket now prices Lula's overall election win at only 16 cents, but Kalshi prices him at 41 to 42 cents and several news outlets describe the runoff as roughly even, so I bought a small Lula position on that gap. I also checked weather forecasts for Chengdu, where multiple sources put the October 5 high near 23 to 26 degrees Celsius, well above the 21 degree threshold one market is betting on, so I bought the No side there. My existing Lula first-round position is already a near-total loss now that the real vote count is in; there is nothing left to do with it since it is not tradeable here, so I am leaving it as is.

trades.reasoning: Official count has Flavio leading Lula by only about 3 points (47 to 44 with 98 percent counted), a much narrower gap than the first partial counts suggested, and multiple post-first-round sources (CNBC, NPR) call the October 25 runoff roughly even while Kalshi prices Lula at 41 to 42 cents. Polymarket's own 16 cent ask looks like an overreaction to the first-round shock headlines rather than a reasoned runoff forecast.

Multiple forecast sources put Chengdu's October 5 high around 23 to 26 degrees Celsius, clearly above the 21 degree threshold this market bets on, so the No side at a 75 cent ask looks underpriced relative to how unlikely an exact 21 degree high is.
